answer.rationale: Two concrete metric declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are directly addressable by inherited signup/onboarding simplification findings (memory_31, memory_86), which are consistent and low-risk relative to the objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but its evidence base is thin—only a four-week readout in the standard SMB segment with no stated measurement of retention, margin, or customer quality over time—raising a real risk that matching a price war could win low-value, price-sensitive accounts at the expense of long-term qualified revenue. I want to verify memory_73's archived record before ever considering a pricing response, and verify memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-simplification result is robust enough to justify committing this week's single experiment slot to it. Given the scarcity of the experiment slot, addressing the clearly measured, directly relevant onboarding decline with a moderate-scale test is the safer, higher-expected-value choice while preserving the option to revisit pricing strategy later with better evidence.
